zoe: Heads-up: after upgrading to @redwood-inference/sdk@1.8.0 our Vercel Edge function started throwing `ReferenceError: process is not defined` and page bundle jumped ~150KB.

omar: that's the classic node-polyfills leak. how are you importing the SDK?

zoe: `import RI from '@redwood-inference/sdk'` from middleware.ts. bundle analyzer shows a CJS wrapper and a node-crypto shim included.

pat: default import hits the legacy `index.js` that does `module.exports = require('./dist/index.cjs.js')`, bundlers collapse it into require and add polyfills.

zoe: checked package.json in node_modules: main + module fields present but no "exports" and no "sideEffects" key.

omar: three options short-term: 1) import explicit ESM build `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/index.esm.js'` 2) pin 1.7.x 3) dynamic import inside edge handler. all are suboptimal.

pat: long-term SDK fixes: add conditional exports map so `import` resolves to ESM, set "sideEffects": false, and move any top-level `require('node:crypto')` into lazy call sites. Also ensure .d.ts covers default export shape for TS.

zoe: repro steps: Next 13 middleware edge, node target=18, esbuild via Next. ci-bot flagged regression: https://ci.internal/artifacts/bundle-1768701234.html

ci-bot: :warning: bundle-size/regression detected (+150KB) for /edge-middleware - artifact uploaded.

omar: also check published tarball: sometimes stray files (maps, extra cjs helpers) cause bundlers to pick up node shims. run `npm pack` locally and inspect.

pat: docs + changelog action: add a short note telling edge/deno/worker users to temporarily import from `dist/index.esm.js` until we publish 1.8.1 with exports map. add a small Next.js edge example.

zoe: I'll open an issue with analyzer HTML and a small repro, assign to @sdk-team and add the changelog draft.

omar: I'll validate PR — will run esbuild + webpack + rollup smoke tests to ensure no node shims in the ESM build.

ci-bot: :white_check_mark: Repro artifact attached to issue #481.
